nodes.name: Substrate Cleaning
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (thickness, 450 μm, Alantum) and carbon paper (thickness, 190 μm, Toray) were cut into 1×3 cm² pieces and partially masked to expose a 1 cm² area at the bottom for electrodeposition. Prior to the electrodeposition, the substrates were ultrasonicated in a diluted 1 M hydrochloric acid solution for least 10 min, rinsed with ethanol and deionized water, and dried in vacuum oven.

nodes.name: Cyclic Voltammetry Electrodeposition of W₁-NiFeOOH
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (8.4 mmol) and Na₂WO₄·2H₂O (0.2 mmol) were dissolved under intensive stirring and ultrasonicated at least 30 min. FeSO₄·7H₂O (2.1 mmol) was added with 30 min stirring. Cyclic electrodeposition from -0.1 to -1.8 V vs Ag/AgCl at 50 mV s⁻¹ for 30 cycles on cleaned Ni foam/carbon paper. Rinsed and dried at 25°C overnight.

nodes.name: MEA Cathode Preparation
nodes.procedure: For the cathode, a catalyst ink was prepared by dispersing PtRu/C in the mixture of isopropanol solution and PiperION ionomer solution, followed by ultrasonication to ensure a homogeneous suspension. This ink was airbrushed onto a PTL-coated carbon paper with a geometric area of 4.4 cm², and the catalyst loading was controlled to reach 1.0 mg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals atomically dispersed W atoms (brighter spots) in the NiFe oxyhydroxide lattice, verified by line intensity profile.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image showing atomically dispersed W atoms in NiFe oxyhydroxide lattice. W atoms with higher atomic number were brighter than Ni or Fe atoms, verified with the line intensity profile (inset).

properties.description: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing atomic structure

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping confirms the atomic distribution of W species in the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic distribution of W species was further confirmed by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines W accounts for an atomic ratio of 2.6% of the total metal content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compositional evaluation using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) determined that W accounted for an atomic ratio of 2.6% of the total metal content.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals single layer W₁–NiFeOOH nanosheet thickness of approximately 4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) images revealed that a single layer of W₁–NiFeOOH nanosheet had a thickness of approximately 4 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns indicate the crystalline structure of electrodeposited pristine (oxy)hydroxides was retained with W incorporation, with diffraction peaks consistent with NiFe (oxy)hydroxide phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns indicated that the crystalline structure of electrodeposited pristine (oxy)hydroxides was retained with the incorporation of single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: W 4f core-level XPS spectra show distinct peaks for W 4f7/2 deconvoluted into W⁵⁺ and W⁶⁺ with electron transfer to the oxyhydroxide host.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The W 4f core-level spectra was showed distinct peaks corresponding to W 4f7/2, which could be deconvoluted into two sets of doublets attributed to W⁵⁺ and W⁶⁺ with electron transfer to the oxyhydroxide host.

nodes.characterization_summary: k³-weighted W L₃-edge FT-EXAFS shows W–O first shell peak at ~1.5-2 Å, no W–W peak confirming atomic dispersion, weak second shell W–Ni/Fe scattering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: k³-weighted W L₃-edge FT-EXAFS spectra in R-space... The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra of W₁–NiFeOOH exhibited a distinct peak for the W–O scattering path in the first shell... absence of a peak corresponding to the first-shell W–W path.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L₃-edge XANES whiteline higher than W foil, aligned with WO₃ (+6 state), higher intensity indicates distorted WO₆ octahedral symmetry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The W L₃-edge XANES spectra of W₁–NiFeOOH showed that the whiteline position was higher than W foil and closely aligned with WO₃... The higher whiteline intensity compared to WO₃ demonstrated a distorted WO₆ octahedral symmetry.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ W L₃-edge XANES shows stable whiteline from OCP to 1.6 V (W valence +5.07→+5.11), confirming W not directly involved in redox during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: normalized in situ W L₃-edge XANES spectra displayed consistent whiteline positions... Average W valence states of +5.07 at OCP and +5.11 at 1.6 V were estimated with a negligible shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows α-to-γ phase transition at 1.43 V with characteristic γ-NiOOH peaks at 474 cm⁻¹ (E_g) and 553 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g}), occurring at lower potential than NiFeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For W₁–NiFeOOH, the spectra revealed a phase transition from the as-prepared α-phase to the OER active γ-phase at 1.43 V, evidenced by the emergence of characteristic Raman peaks at 474 and 553 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the E_g bending and A_{1g} stretching vibration modes of Ni(III)–O in γ-NiOOH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform analysis confirms local atomic structure around W matches substitutional site, not WO₃-like W–O–W scattering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wavelet transform (WT) analysis of EXAFS clarified that the local atomic structure around W atoms was not related to the WO₃ reference peak present in local maximum derived from W–O–W second shell scattering.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman confirms α→γ phase transition at lower potential (1.43 V vs RHE) vs NiFeOOH, with characteristic γ-NiOOH peaks at 474 cm⁻¹ (E_g), 553 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: characteristic peaks related to γ-phase began to appear at lower potentials for W₁–NiFeOOH (1.43 V) compared to both Ir₁–NiFeOOH and NiFeOOH (1.45 V).
